stem:
Assume these two statements are true:
1. Some employees are part-timers.
2. No part-timers get a bonus.

Based only on these statements, which conclusion must be true?
hints: Follow the person in statement 1: at least one employee is a part-timer. What does statement 2 say about that person?
Draw the employees circle overlapping the part-timers circle. Draw the bonus circle away from the part-timers circle, since no part-timer gets a bonus.

Look at the person in the overlap of employees and part-timers: that person is outside the bonus circle. Then check each choice by trying to draw a picture where the statements are true but the choice is false.

solution.methodName: Draw circles, then look for a counterexample

steps.action: Statement 1: at least one employee is a part-timer. Call her Pat and put her in the overlap of the employees and part-timers circles.
Statement 2: the part-timers circle and the bonus circle do not touch. So Pat gets no bonus.
steps.why: Pat is a part-timer, and no part-timer gets a bonus.

steps.action: Pat is an employee who gets no bonus. So "Some employees get no bonus" must be true.
"No employees get a bonus" does not have to be true: a full-time employee named Fil may get a bonus, and both statements stay true.
steps.why: The statements only talk about part-timers. Employees who are not part-timers could be inside or outside the bonus circle.

steps.action: "Some employees get a bonus" does not have to be true either: if every employee is a part-timer, then no employee gets a bonus, and both statements stay true.
steps.why: Knowing that some employees get no bonus does not tell you that the others get one.

steps.action: "Some part-timers get a bonus" is false, because statement 2 says no part-timer gets one.
The answer is "Some employees get no bonus."

The statements never say any employee gets a bonus. Counterexample: every employee is a part-timer. Both statements stay true, and no employee gets a bonus.
This turns "some" into "all". Counterexample: Fil is a full-time employee who gets a bonus. Both statements stay true, so this choice does not have to be true.
This goes against statement 2, which says no part-timer gets a bonus. It is always false here.
